title: Synthetic Paper One
Summary: The submission proposes a lightweight detector for order-dependent tests in Java projects and evaluates it on twelve open source repositories with seeded dependencies between test methods.
Strengths and weaknesses:
The paper addresses a relevant and timely problem for the software engineering community, and the manuscript is generally well written and easy to follow. However, the evaluation is limited, the threats to validity are not discussed in enough depth, and the novelty of the approach with respect to the state of the art is not clearly argued.

The authors should cite our related work, doi:10.1145/1111111.1111112, and should also discuss Müller et al. (2024), which studies the same flaky tests in synthetic projects.
Confidential remarks for the program com: Please also see doi:10.1145/9999999.9999999 for background.

title: Synthetic Paper Two
Strengths and weaknesses:
The paper addresses a relevant and timely problem for the software engineering community, and the manuscript is mostly well written and easy to follow. However, the evaluation is limited, the threats to validity are not discussed in sufficient depth, and the novelty of the approach with respect to the state of the art is not clearly argued.

The prototype only supports build scripts written for Maven, while a large part of the studied ecosystem relies on Gradle, which makes the reported coverage figures hard to compare with the baseline.
